request.spec: Reject creating an owner when another owner has the same lastName and the same address (compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace). Respond with 409, unless the request sets 'sharesHousehold' true.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

Reject creating an owner when another owner has the same lastName and the same address (compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace). Respond with 409, unless the request sets 'sharesHousehold' true.

agent.result_text:
Build succeeds and all tests pass. Here's a summary of the change.

## What I implemented

Creating an owner is now rejected with **409** when another owner shares the same `lastName` **and** `address` (compared case-insensitively, with whitespace runs collapsed) — unless the request sets `sharesHousehold: true`.

Following the project's OfficeFloor function-injection conventions (mirroring the existing `RejectDuplicateTelephone` duplicate check):

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added an optional write-only `sharesHousehold` boolean to the `OwnerFields` schema, so the generated `OwnerFieldsDto` exposes `getSharesHousehold()`.

2. **`RejectDuplicateHousehold`** (new function) — reads the published `@Val OwnerFieldsDto`, short-circuits when `sharesHousehold` is true, otherwise normalizes (`trim` → collapse whitespace → lowercase) `lastName`/`address` and compares against every existing owner, throwing `DuplicateHouseholdException` on a collision.

3. **`DuplicateHouseholdException`** (checked) + **`DuplicateHouseholdHandler`** — responds 409, plus the escalation YAML wiring the handler.

4. **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted the `rejectDuplicateHousehold` step into the pipeline (after the telephone check, before `build`).

The three acceptance tests — rejects same last name + address (409), allows a different address, and allows the duplicate when `sharesHousehold` is set — all pass, and the full suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`).

One design note: because `OwnerFields` is shared with the `Owner` response schema via `allOf`, the generated `OwnerDto` also gains a `sharesHousehold` property; since the `Owner` entity has no such field, MapStruct leaves it unmapped (default WARN policy, no build failure) and it never appears populated in responses. Marking it `writeOnly` keeps its intent as create-only input clear.

probe.probe_text:
Here is the ordered list of everything applied when creating an owner via `POST /api/owners`. The endpoint is defined in `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml` as a nine-step OfficeFloor pipeline.

## Gate (before any step)
- **Authorization** — `composition.authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"`. Without that role the request is rejected 403 (`ForbiddenExceptionHandler`).

## Validations & side-effects, in pipeline order

| # | Step / class | Transaction? | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **RequireOwnerFields** | no | **Validation.** Binds the raw body as `OwnerFieldsDto` (via `@RequestBody`, **not** `@Valid`). Checks required fields present-and-non-blank in this order: `firstName`, `lastName`, `address`, `city`, `telephone`. Any missing → `MissingOwnerFieldsException` → **400**. Republishes the body for later steps. No side effect. |
| 2 | **NormalizeOwnerTelephone** | no | **Validation + mutation.** Normalizes telephone to E.164 (`E164Telephone.normalize`: strip non-digits, drop a leading `0`, prepend country code `61` if no `+`, require 8–15 digits). Invalid → `InvalidTelephoneException` → **400**. Mutates the DTO in place. |
| 3 | **NormalizeOwnerEmail** | no | **Validation + mutation.** Email is optional: null/blank → set to `null`. Otherwise trim + regex-validate; invalid → `InvalidEmailException` → **400**; valid → stored lower-cased. Mutates the DTO. |
| 4 | **RejectDuplicateTelephone** | no | **Validation (read side-effect).** Reads `ownerRepository.findAll()`, compares normalized telephone against every existing owner. Match → `DuplicateTelephoneException` → **409**. Read-only. |
| 5 | **RejectDuplicateHousehold** | no | **Validation (read side-effect).** Skipped if `sharesHousehold == TRUE`. Otherwise reads `findAll()` and compares normalized (trim/collapse-whitespace/lowercase) `lastName` **and** `address`; match on both → `DuplicateHouseholdException` → **409**. Read-only. |
| 6 | **BuildOwner** | **yes** | **Side-effect (in memory).** Maps DTO → `Owner` entity via `OwnerMapper.toOwner` (id, pets, customerCode ignored). If `registrationDate` is null, defaults it to `LocalDate.now()` (today). Publishes the entity. Transaction begins here. |
| 7 | **AssignCustomerCode** | yes | **Side-effect (mutation + read).** Reads `findAll().size()`, computes `sequence = size + 1`, sets `customerCode = "<UP-TO-3-LETTERS-OF-LASTNAME>-<0000 seq>"` (e.g. `SMI-0007`). |
| 8 | **SaveOwner** | yes | **Side-effect — the only DB write.** `ownerRepository.save(owner)`. A constraint breach surfaces as `DataIntegrityViolationException` (handler exists). |
| 9 | **RespondWithOwnerCreated** | yes | **Side-effect (response).** Maps entity → `OwnerDto` (computes `displayName`, `initials`), sends **201 Created** with `Location: /api/owners/{id}`. Transaction commits after this step. |

## Two things worth flagging in the code as it stands

- **Bean-validation constraints on `OwnerFieldsDto` are not enforced.** The DTO carries jakarta annotations (`@NotNull`, `@Pattern`, `@Size` on firstName/lastName/address/city/telephone/email), but step 1 binds with `@RequestBody` **only, no `@Valid`**. So none of those `@Pattern`/`@Size` limits run — all actual validation is the hand-written logic in steps 1–5 (presence, E.164 telephone, email regex, the two duplicate checks). The DTO's telephone `@Pattern("^[0-9]*$")` would in fact reject the normalized `+…` value if it were applied.
- **No entity lifecycle side-effects.** There are no `@PrePersist`/`@PostPersist` callbacks; `registrationDate` and `customerCode` are set explicitly in steps 6–7. `Owner.pets` cascades `ALL`, but `toOwner` ignores `pets`, so creating an owner creates no pets.

I didn't change anything.
